column1: # The shape of every fact the five scanners emit: one row per (scanner, kind),
# naming each field after the kind. rules.py loads this and requires a rule's
# selector to name every field of its kind, so a selector can never be off by
# one column and quietly match nothing.
# Keyed on scanner as well as kind because `error` is not the same fact in all
# five -- ast's carries a line number and the other four do not -- and a rule
# that guessed wrong would be a rule that never fires.

column3: fields (comma separated, in order after the kind)

column1: # `job` is the one probe kind whose key is not the name of a setting: it is
# <label>#<job id>, where <label> is GATE_PROBE_LABEL -- the replay's row name
# -- falling back to the application's own name when nothing set it. A gate
# reads 140 applications' probe files concatenated and job ids restart at 0 in
# each, so the label is what makes a red row attributable to a row; app names
# are not unique here (three mains call themselves CustomReportDemo).
# The value is one of three things, and the third is the point:
#   <id>          the job ran inside SQL execution <id>, which did start
#   -             the job ran outside any execution
#   forged:<id>   the job carried execution id <id> and no such execution ever
